questions.worked_solution:
We need to factor the following expression:

$$
-12{a}^{2}-6a+6
$$

First, notice that all the terms have a common factor of $-6.$ So, we can simplify the calculation by first factoring out $-6:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-6(2{a}^{2}+a-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we just need to factor the trinomial $2{a}^{2}+a-1$ in parentheses. To do this, we find two numbers that 

- multiply to the product of the quadratic coefficient and the constant (which is $2\times (-1)=-2$), and

- add to the linear coefficient (which is $1$).

The factor pairs of $-2$ are

$$
(1,-2),\,(-1,2).
$$

Notice the numbers in the factor pair $(-1,2)$ add to $1:$ 

$$
-1+2=1\,✓
$$

Then, we write the linear term as $-a+2a,$ and factor the result by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{a}^{2}+a-1 & = \\ 2{a}^{2}-a+2a-1 & = \\ (2{a}^{2}-a)+(2a-1) & = \\ a(2a-1)+(2a-1) & = \\ (a+1)(2a-1) & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original trinomial factors as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-12{a}^{2}-6a+6 & = \\ -6(2{a}^{2}+a-1) & = \\ -6(a+1)(2a-1) & \end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $3\le 4x+7\le 19$ or $6x+8<2?$
questions.worked_solution:
We start by solving $3\le 4x+7\le 19:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & \le 4x+7\le 19 \\ -4 & \le 4x\le 12 \\ -1 & \le x\le 3\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252895/assets/7d7303c5608dbd17911794959438f925d7ab6edd3ebba600d657b396ccf8eaa9.png)

Then, we solve $6x+8<2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6x+8 & <2 \\ 6x & <-6 \\ x & <-1\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252895/assets/ad5692ee92c2b67f50c0354020642bd9c711bdf7b88f4d476455512e33f9fc5f.png)

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252895/assets/638b44af1e33b78102a0dbfa3857c1292f200e026f54adf92fe77a97bf7e10a1.png)

Therefore, the final solution is $x\le 3.$

What is the global minimum point of the function shown above?
questions.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following definitions:

- The global minimum of a function is the smallest value that the function attains on its domain. There can only be (at most) one global minimum.

- A global minimum point of a function is a point $(x,y)$ where a function reaches a global minimum. There can be zero, one, or many global minimum points.

For our function, the minimum value reached by the function is $f(x)=-4.$ Therefore, the global minimum is $-4.$ The function reaches this value at $x=2$, so the global minimum point is $(2,-4).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252895/assets/9b5d10eb2ebc424c4096e25dd26af905e9915bfcbeb777471b559280af6fd7ef.png)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252895/assets/a36fe195458e459aea993232a72ed21e0c780135dc4dbe4bece45bfc3b6e50e2.png)

The perimeter of the above triangle is $50+25\sqrt{2}.$ Find the measure of each leg.
questions.worked_solution:
Because the triangle is isosceles, the legs must have the same length. Let $a$ be the length of each leg. So, we have

$$
AB=BC=a.
$$

Moreover, because the triangle is a *right* isosceles triangle, the hypotenuse must be equal to $\sqrt{2}$ times the length of a leg. Therefore,

$$
AC=AB\cdot \sqrt{2}=a\sqrt{2}.
$$

Finally, since the perimeter is $p=50+25\sqrt{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =AB+BC+AC \\ 50+25\sqrt{2} & =a+a+a\sqrt{2} \\ 25(2+\sqrt{2}) & =2a+a\sqrt{2} \\ 25(2+\sqrt{2}) & =(2+\sqrt{2})a \\ 25\cancel{(2+\sqrt{2})} & =\cancel{(2+\sqrt{2})}a \\ 25 & =a\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the measure of a leg is $25.$

questions.worked_solution:
Our goal is to write the equation in the form $ax+by=c,$ where $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors and $a\ge 0.$

We begin by moving all of the variables to the left-hand side and all of the constants to the right-hand side. This gives

$$
-\frac{1}{5}x+y=2
$$

Now, we multiply both sides of the equation by $-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{5}x+y & =2 \\ (-1)\cdot (-\frac{1}{5}x+y) & =(-1)\cdot (2) \\ \frac{1}{5}x-y & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply both sides of the equation by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5}x-y & =-2 \\ 5\cdot (\frac{1}{5}x-y) & =5\cdot (-2) \\ x-5y & =-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors, and $a\ge 0.$ So we are done!

The standard form of the line is $x-5y=-10.$

Remember that $y=|x-h|+k$ is a vertical translation of the absolute value graph $y=|x|$ by $h$ units right and $k$ units up.

Here, the graph is moved left by $4$ units and down by $1$ unit. This corresponds to $h=-4$ and $k=-1.$ So, the equation of the graph is $y=|x+4|-1.$
